mission: Keep Buddy and the DreamCo fleet available as a coordinated 24/7 system using one canonical runtime, durable queues, event-driven workers, schedules, health checks, restart/recovery policy, explicit stop/runtime controls, and a safe idle-improvement loop so every bot continuously looks for lawful revenue opportunities, human productivity improvements, and ways to make Buddy smarter.
truth_boundary: GitHub Actions is CI/orchestration, not a permanent application host. Public repositories can use standard GitHub-hosted Actions without minute charges, but jobs are ephemeral and subject to execution/concurrency limits. 24/7 runtime requires an always-on deployment target or self-hosted runtime.

default_runtime_model.reason: Every bot should be logically available 24/7. When no user or system task is assigned, the scheduler gives the bot bounded background-improvement work instead of wasting a permanent process.

tracks.goal: Find new lawful ways the bot's capability can create measurable economic value for users or DreamCo without making guarantees or taking unapproved financial/external actions.
Find ways to reduce time, cost, clicks, errors, training burden, or repetitive work for humans.
Find verified ways to make Buddy and the fleet smarter, more reliable, easier to use, cheaper, safer, or more capable.

cycle: choose one track relevant to the bot's domain
inspect current benchmarks, gaps, issues, library/model/data freshness, and user-friction evidence
generate a bounded opportunity or improvement hypothesis
search existing canonical implementation to avoid duplicates
score expected user value, revenue/public value, effort, risk, reuse, cost, evidence strength and guardrail fit
if measurable, create or update a benchmark/gap proposal
if reusable, route through shared-fleet improvement inheritance
if implementation is justified, hand off to builder competition rather than self-modifying production
record result, evidence, status and next action
yield immediately when higher-priority work arrives
allowed_without_owner_approval: non-destructive review-branch proposals when repository policy allows
requires_approval: borrowing/lending or applying for financial products
using paid provider runs beyond configured budget
signing agreements or accepting terms on the user's behalf
truth_rules: revenue opportunity is not revenue until money is actually earned and recorded
projected savings are estimates until measured
an idea is not a capability until implemented and verified
a background proposal cannot bypass normal guardrails or owner approval

hosting_strategy.recommended_primary: always-on application/runtime host or managed container/service
hosting_strategy.self_hosted_runner_role: Optional for repository automation that needs your own always-available machine; secure it carefully and do not expose it to untrusted public PR execution.
hosting_strategy.public_github_actions_note: Standard GitHub-hosted runners on public repositories are free for Actions minutes, but are still ephemeral jobs and are not a substitute for Buddy's always-on application runtime.
hosting_strategy.larger_runner_note: Larger GitHub-hosted runners are billed even for public repositories.

fleet_availability_rule: Every verified bot should be logically available through Buddy 24/7. A bot does not need its own permanent process; Buddy routes a task to its canonical capability when requested or scheduled, and assigns safe bounded improvement work when the bot would otherwise be idle.

scheduling_defaults.builder_bots: event-driven from verified gaps/issues plus idle improvement review
scheduling_defaults.benchmark_bots: on code changes plus scheduled refresh
scheduling_defaults.data_discovery: scheduled research windows plus explicit searches
scheduling_defaults.all_verified_bots_idle_mode: rotate through lawful revenue opportunity, human productivity, and Buddy intelligence tracks

shutdown_policy: stop accepting new work for selected scope
allow critical in-flight writes to reach safe checkpoint
guardrails: do not use infinite loops inside GitHub-hosted Actions to imitate permanent hosting
do not restart failing work forever without bounded backoff and dead-letter handling
do not let background work consume unlimited money, bandwidth, storage, battery or provider quota
do not keep expensive GPU/model workers alive while idle unless a measured latency requirement justifies it
do not execute paid/destructive/external actions merely because a bot is always available
do not let background revenue research place trades, spend funds, apply for credit, send outreach, publish, purchase, or change accounts without the required approval
do not create spammy, deceptive, exploitative, unlawful or guaranteed-income opportunity proposals
do not mark a bot 24/7 operational until the deployed runtime and health checks provide evidence
